reviews.text: Östlund has a psychologist’s eye for human nature and the understated comedic touch of Jacques Tati. The end result is akin to virtual slapstick, the emotional equivalent of slipping on a banana peel.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: The film’s execution only occasionally reaches its ideological grasp, but Östlund’s such a talented filmmaker that he can cover up the lack of follow-through in his script. That’s tough to do!
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: The Square foregrounds a dilemma at the core of artistic practice: as moving and influential as it can be, art too often exists in a realm separated from “real life,” cordoned off as safely “consumable” entertainment. —Guest post by Michael Joshua Rowin
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: Sharpened by a series of corrosive comic moments and provocations, The Square lashes out with a refined blow against both indifference and empty gestures of faux-humanitarianism.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: (...) Östlund makes the extension of performativity something that ends up dislodging the meaning, which pierces the artistic itself, until it reaches the Social. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Agustín Acevedo Kanopa

reviews.text: None of the themes explored in this review required much close analysis. Unlike the knife's edge satire of Force Majeure, The Square is a blunt object. But maybe that's what it takes to point out our world's quotidian surrealism...
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Beautifully choreographed and... tweaked but scathingly true to life.
reviews.author: Erin Blackwell

reviews.text: A vision about the high culture and the low culture. The Bourdieu perspective nowadays. A film about our social behavior. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: The Square has been called a satire, likely because we haven't developed a popular term for a film that, though drawn in exaggerated lines, at its foundation is hopeless and doesn't mean to teach us anything with its hopelessness.
reviews.author: Seph Rodney

reviews.text: As much as The Square enjoys poking fun at the buffoonery of the art world, it's more interested in what that world represents: a self-sustaining bubble where money, power, and posturing commingle.
reviews.author: Craig Hubert

reviews.text: The reason why The Square works so brilliantly with macabre and laughter is that it mirrors what we see and do everyday.
reviews.author: Katie Hogan

reviews.text: The Square is a bit too cynical for its own good, but reaffirms my belief that the future of cinema can be found in Scandinavia.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: [A] wickedly funny and insightful film.
reviews.author: Felicia Feaster

reviews.text: Ostlund latest satire is as formidably funny as it is a harsh condemnation of estranged humanity.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: The Square is a bizarre film that has it's moments and Claes Bang is very good at playing suave but awkward.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: It can be noted that it wants to offer a more global approach, but this is not the feeling that end up being transmitted, and it is a shame. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: With bright moments, 'The Square' seems right and necessary. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sara Martínez Ruiz

reviews.text: Don't they know it's the end of the world?
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Christian is the affluent chief curator of an elitist Stockholm art museum preparing to mount an exhibition called "The Square" when he is robbed of his phone, his wallet and, incredibly, his cufflinks.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Ostlund's film carries bizarre and hilarious edges.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: A film that is merely good when it should have been great, insisting on holding our hands and asking "do you get it?" rather than allowing its brilliantly bitter wit to speak for itself.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: The Square is not really saying something new but it is making its points in a strikingly fresh, satiric way.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: The Square is actually the sum of its parts, rather than a seamless whole. Viewers are probably going to pick differing scenes as their favourites.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: Delightfully unhinged; a viewing experience that can't be conveniently collapsed into review-friendly phrases like "precocious art world satire" or "modern morality play". The Square is both of these things, and more.
reviews.author: Rachel Brook

reviews.text: Regardless of its long duration and wacky side, there are genius moves and several engrossing parts...
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: This is a finely honed machine that hits a perfect blend of thoughtful and intellectual commentary, while also being impossible to pry your eyes away from, minute by minute.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: Swedish writer-director Ruben Ostlund creates an ingenious high-wire act putting bourgeois beliefs and interpersonal trust to the test in THE SQUARE.
reviews.author: Rania Richardson

reviews.text: A terrific exemplar of ambitious cringe comedy, executed with great assurance and wit.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: The Square shows the good condition - powerful and ruthless - of Östlund's creativity, a filmmaker capable of making a world full of comedy that is sometimes dislocated by something totally mysterious or intensely visceral. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: Östlund is questioning the very function of art and while we can read the film in myriad ways, it's unlikely that we're supposed to choose one interpretation.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: The film runs the risk of becoming an exercise in the very thing it deigns to mock - bourgeois, middlebrow values.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Östlund asking [his social questions] seeks inciting a reaction and yet my experience watching The Square was one of indifference instead.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: This is a good movie. A masterpiece for the ages? Probably not. But a sardonic commentary on contemporary art and society.
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

reviews.text: You won't forget it in a hurry, but you may never come to understand it.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: A sharp-edged, funny, original, and often thoughtful approach to the connection between art to life.
reviews.author: Monica Reid

reviews.text: Östlund's...world, though basically satiric, is also rooted in what's believable about the obsessions of contemporary society - not just in Sweden but Europe-wide. When does tolerance of others become simply indifference?
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: The Square is often humorless and just as arrogant as its lead character. Relevant themes such as economic inequality, media sensationalism and institutional rot are pummeling and obvious.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: The Square uses both comedic and dramatic elements to illustrate the ways we, and our various creations and institutions, fail one another.
reviews.author: Deborah Krieger

reviews.text: A gentle critique, peopled with eccentric but likeable characters, those who have the warmth and the humanity to redeem themselves.
reviews.author: Namrata Joshi

reviews.text: Remarkably thoughtful, and also rather harrowing.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: As intelligent and well assembled as The Square is, it lets its audience off the hook with a wink at every turn.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: At times a searing social commentary, the darkly funny The Square is an indictment of the decadence of upper-middle-class inner city liberals and their cluelessness to everyone outside of their privileged bubbles.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Though it goes on a bit and loses its way in places, this funny and occasionally disturbing satire of the art world is a deserving winner.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: The Square is undeniably entertaining, though its lasting use may be to demonstrate that movies can have the same effect as popping a coin in the collecting tin. Having seen the film, you can rest easy knowing you've already given.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: The main problem is that it takes potshots at about everything that is wrong with society. You feel like you're watching a subject taking shape in the creator's mind and then being abandoned for something else...the acting is world-class, however.
reviews.author: Devesh Sharma

reviews.text: A film as funny as it is stingingly accurate about the way in which the digital era encourages us to perform altruism whilst sheltering our private vanities and resentments.
reviews.author: Tom Duggins

reviews.text: The Square is long but that's not a criticism because it's never dull and manages to pack in some spectacularly unlikely set pieces.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: It's easy to dismiss The Square as a good-looking but over-extended art-house muddle. But those with the stamina to stick with Ruben Ostlund's [film] may find some of its themes staying with them.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: It gives Dadaists a dose of their own medicine.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Östlund at his best can have his cake and push it in your face.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Like Bobby McFerrin and Yo-Yo Ma's oddly off-kilter rendition of Ave Maria, which echoes throughout the drama, The Square is a strange mix of pop and profundity: archly entertaining, occasionally grating and consistently uncomfortable.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Ostlund uses his setting to explore hidden inequalities in supposedly liberal societies, particularly those concerning masculinity, race and class, playing with our expectations about what is supposed to happen versus the uncomfortable results.
reviews.author: Violet Lucca

reviews.text: A satire gleefully poking fun at the pretensions of the art world and liberal Swedes' earnest efforts to promote a dialogue on immigration and racism.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: The Square is a fiercely witty comedy that requires and rewards patience from us...but there is also something blunt and ill-conceived about The Square's central thrust....the film is principally a social critique, but it's heavy-handed, even moralistic.
reviews.author: Edward Lawrenson

reviews.text: With The Square, writer-director Ruben Ostlund finally lives up to the potential seen in his previous films.
reviews.author: Aakash Karkare

reviews.text: ... an astoundingly smart film...
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Swedish writer-director Ruben Ostlund follows-up his memorably compelling 2014 relationship drama-cum-cringe-comedy Force Majeure with another thought-provoking meditation on modern social mores.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: A bracingly original satire that highlights the growing divide between rich and poor and the failings of modern man.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: Like director Ruben Östlund's last movie, the phenomenal Force Majeure, his new one, The Square, is a bitingly hilarious satire about masculinity, and about the lies men tell themselves.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: The Square picks at some pretty low-hanging fruit, but there's fun to be had in the way it interrogates the moral commitment of artists and institutions intent on making great social claims for their work.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Östlund repeatedly picks apart our perception of class, race and self-righteousness. Along with Claes Bang, Elisabeth Moss, Dominic West and Terry Notary, he creates an uncomfortable experience on multiple levels, infused with dark comedy.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: The Square is recommended viewing but only for the truly eclectic.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: In spite of its lengthy running time and the darkness of its themes, the film is frequently very funny.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Östlund is a clever, dazzling misanthrope.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: Ultimately, the philosophy at play is just too shallow and simplistic. Best viewed under the categories 'addictive sensationalism' or 'sophisticated, accelerated soap.'
reviews.author: Paddy Kehoe

reviews.text: Another dazzling film by Sweden's Ruben Östlund.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Pondering everything from free expression and sexual harassment to bourgeois guilt and migrant rage, this superbly acted saga may not always hit the target. But it unerringly leaves its mark.
reviews.author: David Parkinson

reviews.text: It illustrates, with great patience and wit, something I once read that the artist Kurt Schwitters wrote: "Banality is bourgeois style."
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Gloriously cynical and delightfully slapstick - take from it what you will.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Describing this as a film about art would be like describing Casablanca as a film about running a bar.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: Östlund definitely takes a few pot shots at pretension, but he lets his comically-barbed scenarios meander into other unexpected territories.
reviews.author: Tony Stamp

reviews.text: There's much here to enjoy, from Moss' funny performance to some gags during a virtual cameo by Dominic West...It's a sometimes lushly cinematic saga that makes heavy (if sometimes awkward) points about all sorts of pressing contemporary topics.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: The film is peculiar, funny and baffling, but never superficial. It delves into class, power and cowardice in a similar vein to Force Majeure.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: When Östlund hits his stride, boy does this film snap and crackle, shooting all kinds of sparks - aesthetic, thematic, sub-textual, conceptual, postmodern, primordial - all in sorts of directions.
reviews.author: Luke Buckmaster

reviews.text: The Square is littered with dramatic confrontations and struggles that make it engaging and accessible to a wider audience without undermining its thoughtfulness or ability to take outlandish risks and pull them off.
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: At its best, it skims sublimely from scene to scene, arousing constant knowing humour, satirical appreciation and - Östlund's speciality - ambiguous dread, before arriving at the scene of the year.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: The Square is satire at its finest and a hilarious takedown of snobbery and elitism.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: The script is witty, the performances flawless, the ideas - mostly - profound.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: The Square is not a film that says superficial things, or says them in a simple way. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: A seriously oddball piece of work...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: If that sounds lofty, this is more surreal japery than suave satire. It plays out at times more like an arthouse-Jackass or a cringe-comedy made chucklingly icky-odd.
reviews.author: Brian Gibson

reviews.text: An "intelligent, ingenious" movie (as Agnès Jaoui, member of the jury) stated. Joyful and critical, we should add. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: Unmissable.
reviews.author: Mark Demetrius

reviews.text: Although it lasts more than two hours, it flows quite well, replete with incredible performances and a story that feels almost like a direct attack. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Díaz Reyes

reviews.text: The total is very much the sum of its terrific parts, although the film could, in all honesty, be a little shorter.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund's The Square is a much more goofier affair, an entertaining but episodic satire on the pretentious nature of the modern art industry.
reviews.author: Alex Lines

reviews.text: The Square keeps viewers off-balance, taking on race and xenophobia, gender and abuse, poverty and class privilege with a sideways Nordic tone that is both hilarious and serious.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Yet, this movie is anything but misanthropic. And while it pokes at the pretensions of modern art, it does not dismiss it altogether.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Presenting itself as a balanced satire of everyone, Östlund's "I hate all people equally" take is never satisfying.
reviews.author: Chelsea Phillips-Carr

reviews.text: The movie makes the audience laugh while looking covering its eyes in embarrassment for the characters. [Full review in Portuguese.]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Brilliant satire on the art world focused on the pretentious, Whitney Museum milieu in Sweden. A morality tale mixed with sketches that put SNL to shame.
reviews.author: Louis Proyect

reviews.text: Largely functions as a laundry list of scene concepts.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A funny comedy about modern art, upper class smugness and how thin the veneer of civilization is. It also has plot elements that don't fit together, and the movie's beginning and end seemed way too far apart.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: But whether The Square is a masterpiece or complete garbage (or both?), at the very least, it's a pleasure to see a talented, confident filmmaker so committed to thinking outside the box.
reviews.author: Lawrence Garcia

reviews.text: The Square is not especially subtle or groundbreaking, but its presentation is often quite novel. If you can manage the odd pacing and the loose plot, there is quite a bit of dark humor amid the discomfort.
reviews.author: Al Hoff

reviews.text: An examination of social context, elitism, cultural bubbles and more, The Square is - to put it precisely - absolutely bonkers. But purposefully bonkers.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: Östlund fills his film with uncomfortable moments - off-screen noises, crying babies, and one confounding sequence involving an artiste impersonating an ape - but it's all in service of an idea: Hypocrisy, thy name is the 21st century.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: The final act is where the film weaves a few of these zany scenarios into something far more complex that asks Christian deep moral questions, and by extension demands the audience to juxtapose all of it with their own lives
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The Square is further proof that we have an admirably ferocious social critic in [director Ruben] Östlund. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Krauze

reviews.text: The Square stands as a triumph of ambition that results in a wildly mixed achievement, water balloons dropped by a prankish director on the art world's many targets of opportunity.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: ... In this bitter anecdote, Robert Östlund shakes the foundation of capitalist perfection through the moral abuse he exerts on his flawed characters by letting them know exactly that, that they aren't perfect. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Unusual, ambiguous and brilliant, Ruben Östlund's tragicomedy about contemporary art is one of the major films of 2017. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Huidobro

reviews.text: This slow-starting film picks up speed and action to effectively show the layers of racism in social relationships and the chaos caused by our own inconsistencies in how we see other people.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: This is one movie that still will have you thinking about it long after the final credits roll.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: The film's wild ambition is commendable, but it doesn't handle all of the challenges so capably
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Elisabeth Moss, Dominic West, and Terry Notary bring their A games to complex roles.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: The whole experience is rough going: sometimes numbing, sometimes horrifying, sometimes merely baffling. There's a kind of artful artlessness at work here
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund's dark comedy-drama The Square starts as a satire on the modern-art world -- a big fish in a small barrel -- but grows into a stinging examination of how well, or how poorly, we treat our fellow human beings.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: [Director Ruben] Östlund's skewering of passive modern culture and our instinct for self-preservation is both relentless and instantly relatable.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: It deals with topics such as modern art, the trivialization and bastardization of journalism, the homeless, racism. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: 'The Square' makes you uncomfortable; it is off-putting, which may be (director Ruben) Ostlund's intention.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: ... this tense high-society takedown remains taut, gawk-worthy, and thought-provoking, to say the least.
reviews.author: Craig Takeuchi

reviews.text: A forceful film that doesn't disappoint. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José C. Donayre Guerrero

reviews.text: The Square is a bold study of human selfishness and vulnerability, fully aware that the world today moves so fast, shouts so loud, and is unstable in a way that we haven't witnessed in recent history.
reviews.author: Yasmin Shehab

reviews.text: It has it's charm. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Phillipp Engel

reviews.text: It works well as a cocktail of light reflections on the hypocrisy of society, but it does not probe rigorously into anything. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jaime Fa de Lucas

reviews.text: Has many brilliant moments.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: It's a satirical, wild ride. It's ART!
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Again and again, Ostlund returns to the theme of human behavior, and the uneasy comedy that can result when so-called civilized people are pushed out of their comfort zones. The iconic image in an Ostlund film is a nervous, frozen little smile.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Given the relationship of the installation to the film and the film to the installation, it's impossible for one work not to overcloud one's view of the other.
reviews.author: Josh Cabrita

reviews.text: While Ostlund's reach sometimes exceeds his grasp, it's unsettling, even confusing, but also captivating.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Featuring a number of jaw-dropping sequences, "The Square" bites hard on social mores exposing the inherent hypocrisy associated with some of the loudest voices sounding the political correctness alarm.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Clearly, Östlund is reaching for more than a straightforward character/morality study with The Square, but in the process of looking for more, the movie loses its way.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: It's funny throughout - not to say that it inspires many laughs, but it's full of irony and absurdity and is very smart.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A sly parable of white privilege brought low.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: In its defense, "The Square" raises serious questions about wealth and poverty, about the power of images, about our responsibilities to people in need. And those are questions that are as relevant today as they've ever been.
reviews.author: Charles Ealy

reviews.text: For me the excitement waned as the film got into the last stages of its 142-minute run time, but until then it fulfills the requirements of an arthouse roller-coaster ride.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: As overindulgent as it is, The Square is a darkly humorous and horrific mirror to our culture.
reviews.author: Josh Kupecki

reviews.text: Perhaps a tighter edit was in order, but commitment is rewarded with biting social commentary and satire, and a necessary pantsing of the contemporary art scene.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: It's unconventional and, at times, startling, but it's far from vapid. Because of it, the film flies by despite its hefty running time, and it has plenty of staying power to boot.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: [The Square is] funny, has an act that turns a person's world and family upside down, has lots of uncomfortable situations, and uses a dash of surrealism.
reviews.author: Charles Mudede

reviews.text: [The Square] covers more than it can grasp, but its satire is almost always hilarious. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nando Salvá

reviews.text: Christian is just the right amount of the discernibly awful to highlight our own awfulness, and The Square is exactly the parody we need to address it.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: To be clear, the film is definitely more good than bad, but [Ruben] Östlund has set a high bar for himself, and this could have been a lot more by being a lot less.
reviews.author: Shawn Hazelett

reviews.text: It's a far cry from Östlund's last film, the marvelous, men-are-chickens comedy "Force Majeure." What's missing this time is any real sense of drama.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: a witty, if somewhat obvious, art world set satire examining the 'bystander effect,' humankind's willingness to help a stranger in need decreasing the larger the crowd is. Bang is perfection in the lead role...
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It gazes disturbingly, absurdly head-on as humans unused to conflict find themselves challenged.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: As in his previous film Force Majeure, Ostlund has identified malaises in modern life. And he has layered questions about them, by the way ordinary situations turn absurd
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund's ('Force Majeure') latest feature is a blistering satire of the modern art world, and features a sequence that will make your jaw completely drop.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: It's laugh-out-loud funny and occasionally just plain silly. But it asks a serious question that seems more urgent with every passing day: "How much inhumanity does it take before we access your humanity?"
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Between the long running time, a few loose ends, and a random bonobo in Moss's apartment, The Square doesn't deliver the kind of concentrated thinking person's entertainment as Östlund's previous film.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: 152 minutes is an awful lot of this.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: For all its stylishness and sophistication, "The Square" never adds up to more than its very attractive parts.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Östlund's craft is immaculate, his range ambitious, his shifts of tone breathtaking.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Östlund gets at the what makes a movie like 'The Square' seem even more provocative than it is: We love the idea that art should be confrontational. But we don't really like to be confronted by it.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Bold, bizarre, and outrageously funny, but repetitive and occasionally drags.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Swedish director Ruben Ostlund's art-world satire is frustratingly hit-and-miss. But when it hits, this slapstick tragedy will knock the wind out of you.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: At what point do you become engaged with what is happening around you and what is the causal effect
reviews.author: Neely Swanson

reviews.text: The good parts of The Square - and there are quite a few of them - can't overcome the weaknesses, making this a decidedly mixed bag.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The Square is probably the film of the year - though that's not necessarily a good thing.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: There are many movies that aim to be both funny and philosophically astute, and most tend to be wild misfires. The Square isn't one of them.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: ... the movie effectively eviscerates the recognizably high-minded aloofness that defines them.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: Language, sex, violence in award-winning dark comedy.
reviews.author: Michael Ordoña

reviews.text: These questions of social action/inaction are certainly topical given our current political climate, but are Östlund's machinations too existential?
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: This is a sly social satire that demands patience from its audience, but like last year's Toni Erdmann, there are ample rewards for those who stay the course. I wish The Square was shorter, but its major set pieces are brilliant.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: The Square, where the enlightened and well-heeled are always gliding past beggars, remains a potent satire.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: [A] wickedly funny film, which is mostly about a feeling problem-the gap between what we think we feel, as kind and caring people, and the deeds we actually do.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The argument in favor of The Square is not that it's great fun to watch, but that it's very entertaining to ponder after viewing. It lingers, both amusingly and disturbingly.
reviews.author: Mark Jenkins

reviews.text: It's a satire keeps the camera rolling after the punchline to allow time for the full, uncomfortable implication of the joke to settle.
reviews.author: Keith Phipps

reviews.text: Lands its bullseyes, over and over, with a faultless precision that grows duller with each strike.
reviews.author: Inkoo Kang

reviews.text: "The Square" is ultimately a long version of Christian's rambling apology, ostentatiously smart, maybe too much so for its own good, but ultimately complacent, craven and clueless.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Writer-director Ruben Ostlund can get a little surreal, most unsettlingly when the bizarre image or situation he's put on screen makes you think, hmm, that could actually happen.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: It affirms that art, this movie very much included, can tell us things about ourselves that we'd prefer not to know.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: It tries so hard to tweak the audience, it virtually breaks a sweat.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: Navigating the nexus of hype, commerce, ego, and bullshit that drives the modern art scene, The Square is almost too perfect in its cunning simplicity.
reviews.author: Blake Goble

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund's latest film skewers artists and their patrons, immigrants and natives, and even the homeless. But it exemplifies the kind of middle-class, middle-brow, liberal intellectualism it's supposed to be mocking.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: The Square delivers a savage satire on the international art world.
reviews.author: Christian Lorentzen

reviews.text: [Ruben Östlund] is also a very effective filmmaker who see things happen in situations that seem to have nothing happening. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Quim Casas

reviews.text: If the film has any flaw, it could be that it juggles too many good ideas. But why complain about that?
reviews.author: Geoff Andrew

reviews.text: The Square at times feels more like longform performance art than a narrative film. It's social satire by way of art-world comedy, and no woke participant is exempt from its barbs.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: The Square is a delight, a masterclass in anxiousness and discomfort pitted towards intellectual exploration.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: The Square is both outlandishly funny and biting-and features a fascinating and sometimes disturbing performance by Terry Notary.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: The genius of [Ruben] Östlund's writing, and his careful staging of each major set piece, is that he's never inviting the audience to sit back and simply laugh at the ridiculousness.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: But in all its flawed brilliance, The Square remains an original, visceral, uncomfortable and essential viewing experience.
reviews.author: Lee Marshall

reviews.text: [Ruben] Ostlund is a master at showing the ways in which we are all bumbling fools at heart; his cinema is a symphony of awkward interactions and stupid mistakes, building to a crescendo of ineptitude.
reviews.author: Steve Pond

reviews.text: Point and laugh all you like but beware, The Square is a schadenfreude boomerang.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: We have the skeleton of a great film smothered in too many layers of fat and gristle.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: This Palme d'Or winner is a meaty film of ideas with instant-classic set-pieces and moments of mind-blowing freakiness, a stunning follow-up to Force Majeure.
reviews.author: Erica Abeel

reviews.text: Any compassionate gestures toward the lower depths of society, with nicely composed shots of the homeless on the street, feel too flimsy to carry critical weight.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: The sharply observed, wryly funny work for addresses difficult questions about race and class that most people usually just whisper about.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: The Square is an art installation outside the museum, a little zone in which "we all share equal rights and obligations," and that concept informs much of the film's satire.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: What other filmmaker could get away with giving Moss' character a chimpanzee for a flatmate and never commenting on it?
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: 'The Square' is unlike anything you've seen before
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Östlund's script becomes painfully drawn out, aching to build to a fulfillment that never really comes. This all partnered with a long runtime that feels both obnoxious and unnecessary.
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: Here is a lazy satire unworthy of a sneeze from such masters of the form as Lars von Trier. Perhaps one day Ruben Östlund will make a competent film; don't hold your breath.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Despite being 2.5 hours long, The Square is often bitingly original, and as a whole well worth the watch.
reviews.author: David Fontana

reviews.text: In scene after exquisitely staged scene, it threatens to put too fine a point on otherwise thrillingly indeterminate situational comedy.
reviews.author: Carson Lund

reviews.text: The Square's narrative is meandering and episodic, feeling almost like a feel-bad sketch comedy show than a traditional story.
reviews.author: Andrew Todd

reviews.text: As thought-provoking as it is hilarious.
reviews.author: Britt Hayes

reviews.text: The Square is a brilliant examination of the motivations of our own personal morality, and a truly amazing comedy.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: It's a visually striking, well-performed film that some people will adore and others will hate. I suspect it will be divisive, kind of like all great art, and I think that's exactly how Ostlund wants it.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: The Square turns from a sharp art-world satire into something egregiously bonkers, a mish-mash of blunt comic beats and heavy-handed social commentary.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: [Ruben] Östlund's provocative, keenly observed take on the contemporary art world is compulsively watchable.
reviews.author: Paul Ennis

reviews.text: An acerbic, entertaining, surreal and statement-making portrait.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A potent, disturbing work that explores the boundaries of political correctness, artistic liberty and free speech in provocative ways.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: The centrepiece sequence, which occurs about halfway through, is a veritable tour de force.
reviews.author: Giovanni Marchini Camia

reviews.text: Bang delivers an incredible performance, his highly-strung and intensely self-important character constantly undermining the altruistic message at the heart of the story.
reviews.author: Gemma Pecorini Goodall

reviews.text: For all its caustic wit, The Square is a fiercely moral film. It knows wrong from right.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: The Square contains many pleasures, as well as the single most extraordinary scene I have seen all year ...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Like Michael Haneke with a funny bone instead of a magnifying glass, Ruben Östlund's vision of humanity is a bleak, almost faithless caricature of our most craven impulses. Nonetheless, there is truth in his perspective.
reviews.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

reviews.text: The film isn't as round as its previous work, but preserves the inherent seal of the director's filmography. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oscar Uriel

reviews.text: It's unfortunate that the film closes with much weakness and uses its best material in the first part. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: There's a wonderful character study lurking within the confines of these vignettes, but Ostlund drifts between them in an unwieldy running time that never justifies its heft.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: The film itself, two hours and 20 minutes long, would have benefited from a greater sense of the economy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: The situations become intolerable because of their length, the jokes are as fancy as not very effective. I have no complicity with Ostlund's sense of humor. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: The Square lives fueled by anger, by the need to tell everything on every plane, to overcome by accumulation. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: A sagacious criticism of artistic snobbery full of absurd pretensions. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: Östlund is specific and exacting as a writer and director, and within The Square's empty spaces, we're forced to confront our own values, and our own visions of ourselves.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: The result is somewhat disappointing because Östlund's talent got buried by a pretentious accumulation of "performances"[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: The film's approach could be interesting if it weren't because it tries to tackle too many things in more than two and a half hours of footage without them fit at all. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: At its best, a turbulent subterranean river of uneasiness and sordidness beating under inventive and even disparate comedy records. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos F. Heredero

reviews.text: It doesn't have the pure weapon-like clarity of Östlund's previous film Force Majeure. But it sets out to make your jaw drop. And it succeeds.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Most of the film's best scenes could function as their own short film; string enough of them together and they all shed different light on a central theme, though never quite fully articulating it.
reviews.author: Emily Yoshida

reviews.text: This is a movie with a lot on its mind, from art to altruism to the so-called bystander effect, and it could function as a Rorschach test for its audience, reflecting viewers' anxieties and insecurities right back at them.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Ostlund, at his best, is a heady and enthralling filmmaker, but unfortunately, he has so much on his mind that he is also, at his weakest, a shapeless and didactic one.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: At times the film feels overly episodic and pleased with itself but this is a sharp and skilful dissection of bourgeois hypocrisies that resonates all too uncomfortably.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

synopsis: Disaster strikes when a curator hires a public relations team to build some buzz for his renowned Swedish museum.
